algorithm.title: Diagnostic Algorithm for the Patient with Leukocytosis.

cell.label: History, physical exam, and complete blood count with automated differential
White blood cell count more than 11,000 with no clear signs of infection?
No further hematologic evaluation needed; treat infection.
See Table 1 for differential diagnosis by cell type.

Myeloblasts: lymphoma or leukemia Lymphoblasts: lymphoma or leukemia Auer rods: acute myelogenous leukemia Small B-cells with cleaved nuclei: Follicular lymphoma Villous projections: splenic marginal zone lymphoma Hyperlobulated nuclei: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma Cerebriform nuclei: Sezary Cells in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma Leukoerythroblastic smear: myelophthisic bone marrow Smudge cells: chronic lymphocytic leukemia Organisms within WBC's: overwhelming sepsis Ragged cytoplasm: hairy cell leukemia.
May need further evaluation with bone marrow biopsy depending on clinical presentation and clinical suspicion.
Bone marrow biopsy to confirm diagnosis and Hematology consult.
